subject: music
topicName: free composition and composing to a brief

steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Free composition allows you to choose your own starting point — a melody, chord progression, rhythm or concept that inspires you. | Key Fact: Composing to a brief requires interpreting AQA's stimulus: read carefully, identify the musical implications, plan how you will respond to each element. | Key Fact: Both compositions must be at least 1 minute each — the score must be in staff notation (up to 4 sharps/flats) with a recording. | Key Fact: AO2 marks: technical control (accuracy of notation, appropriate writing for instruments), coherence (logical structure, development), creative development (inventive use of elements).

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe how free composition and composing to a brief are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary. | Compare how two different pieces use free composition and composing to a brief. Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use free composition and composing to a brief in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.
